audience.programmeDescription: Nanobiology is an English-taught joint bachelor from TU Delft and Erasmus University Rotterdam. It combines biology, physics and mathematics to investigate living systems at small scales, with laboratory, computational and imaging work. A minor, electives and a final research project complete the programme.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme studies living systems through molecular and laboratory biology, evolution, quantitative methods and physical foundations. The second emphasises disease, immunity and organ-system function. Delft and Erasmus provide more specialised nanoscale biophysics, microscopy and instrumentation.

concepts: Investigate biomolecules, cells and living systems through laboratory biology, evolution, mathematical and computational modelling, and physical and chemical foundations. Molecular disease and drug mechanisms provide biological applications; specialist nanoscale measurement remains a limitation.

Prioritise molecular and cellular disease mechanisms, pharmacology, immunity and organ-system consequences, supported by laboratory biology and quantitative methods. Additional brain and perception foundations support biological function; physical, evolutionary and advanced algorithmic specialisation have less weight.
blockHeadings: Scientific computation and biological data methods

selectedNote.text: The UCR programmes combine molecular and cellular biology, laboratory work and quantitative methods. The first adds evolution and physical/chemical foundations; the second gives more weight to disease, immunity and biological function. Specialist nanoscale biophysics, microscopy acquisition, electronic instruments and soft-matter training remain limitations. These are related academic programmes rather than full Nanobiology equivalence.

selectedCourseDescriptions.name: Personal & Professional Development
selectedCourseDescriptions.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
